acceptedAnswer.text: By the strict textbook definition, percent error is the absolute value and so never negative. Many labs keep the sign to show direction: negative means your measurement is below the accepted value, positive means above. Switch the Sign setting to choose.

mainEntity.name: What is an acceptable percent error?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the field and the purpose. A teaching lab may accept a few percent, while precision manufacturing or analytical chemistry may require well under 1%. Use the tolerance check with the limit your course, standard or specification sets.

mainEntity.name: What if the theoretical value is zero?

acceptedAnswer.text: Percent error is undefined because it divides by the accepted value. Report the absolute error with its units instead, or use an absolute tolerance in the tolerance check.
Round only the final answer, not the intermediate steps. The significant-figures setting rounds the displayed results; the calculation itself always uses full precision.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between percent error and percent difference?

acceptedAnswer.text: Percent error compares a measurement with an accepted reference value and divides by that value. Percent difference compares two measurements when neither is a reference and divides by their average.

mainEntity.name: Why is percent error not the same as uncertainty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Percent error needs a known accepted value, whereas uncertainty describes the doubt in the measurement itself. A percent error smaller than the measurement uncertainty means the result agrees with the accepted value within what the measurement can resolve.
